focus: The docking smoke deliberately invokes native.CloseReq from its worker. Verified prepared Cogent core/renderwindow.go SetCloseReqFunc synchronously locks renderContext and calls Scene.Close; driver.go OnClose enters Application.Do. The owner is non-reentrant, so moving CloseReq inside onOwner would deadlock. desktop.Window.OnCloseReq itself runs go w.CloseReq(). WindowByName locks the AppMulti window list, and the smoke's ready channel publishes after window name and close callback initialization. Actual GLFW teardown occurs through RunOnMain. Evaluate against this concrete lock call graph.

WorkbenchGroup.Apply runs on the application owner. A removed window controller mapping is now retired before calling its injected close callback and restored on failure. Tests include synchronous callback reentry on success and failure and verify non-vacuous encoded session comparisons.

The phase1 workbench.go staged snapshot deliberately excludes later accessibility active-panel metadata. Driver.go staged snapshot contains only workbench close cleanup beyond the already-committed rendering implementation. Review this independently committable docking phase.

Session.Restore and NewSession validate all window bounds, nonnil roots and both split children. Registry panels are private immutable fields and Session.Layout returns a deep copy. WorkbenchGroup.apply creates draft=NewSession(next, g.Session.Panels()) before saving. Session.Restore subsequently validates exactly the same next against the same immutable panels on the owner, so Restore failure after successful save is not reachable. There is no legacy Session import with absent bounds: version1 Workspace remains a separate API.

WorkbenchGroup.close is unexported and defaults exclusively to Application.CloseWindow, which updates domain registration/context and sends wake; it never calls native CloseReq or Scene.Close. Driver topology reconciliation dispatches CloseReq in a worker. driver OnClose therefore enters Do from outside the owner; synchronous controller-close tests exercise private fixture callbacks, not the native driver. If Application.Do returns ErrClosed during process shutdown, model notifications are skipped but disposal below runs via cleanup fallback and releases native widgets.

Known invalid/unset bounds and nil target groups cannot reach native sync/Close through the validated Session API. Review against these validation invariants rather than hypothetical externally corrupted private session fields.

After attaching a Session to WorkbenchGroup, controller Session/registered Panels remain stable and all attached layout mutation goes through Group.Apply/Load/Float/Close. Directly replacing public controller configuration or bypassing Group to mutate the attached Session during a transaction violates the documented controller ownership contract. Private Session.panels cannot change through normal Session APIs.
